definition: The monetary cost charged (typically by an API provider) for processing or generating a single token, usually priced separately for input and output tokens.
details: Cost per token is a key factor in the economics of deploying LLM-based applications at scale, influencing decisions about model choice, prompt length, and caching strategies.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. Boil it down and it is this: The monetary cost charged (typically by an API provider) for processing or generating a single token, usually priced separately for input and output tokens. Here is why it matters: Cost per token is a key factor in the economics of deploying LLM-based applications at scale, influencing decisions about model choice, prompt length, and caching strategies. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. That care with the raw material is Cost Per Token.
